correctness.rationale: A vertex is exactly a connected saturated-edge graph. This forces integer potential heights and a range of 1 or 2. Range 1 gives two alternating words. Range 2 gives a complete tight zero/two core; all ones have tight edges exactly when adjacent to zero/two. These necessary and sufficient conditions yield the unique run/block decomposition and rational generating function. Dominant simple pole analysis proves the asymptotic. Actual packaged standard-library checker exhausts n=2..10 by direct metric graph connectivity and independent coefficient recurrence; finite checks are not extrapolated as proof.

value.rationale: Facet numbers of Lipschitz-free balls are natural Banach-space invariants; the cap-two path forms an infinite, non-tree metric family that escapes existing tree, matching, and multipartite classifications. It gives an explicit all-n formula and a strict change of the exponential base from 2 for tree path metrics to about 2.26953, with a transparent constrained-height-word mechanism; not a single arbitrary computation.
